recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for FHIR-3832. Future changes should wait for a final PA/FHIR-I decision if the newer compartment membership questions need different patient-vs-subject behavior.
issue_request: FHIR-3832 was a Published/Persuasive PA change request asking for an Appointment patient/subject search parameter so appointments could be retrieved for a patient and included in compartment-style queries.
initial_application: No explicit git commit mentioning FHIR-3832 was found. The current source rewrite history carries an Appointment-patient SearchParameter, and later Appointment work expanded it to cover both patient participant actors and patient-valued Appointment.subject references.
additional_context: Appointment is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-14803 later rejected adding a separate Appointment.patient element and explicitly relied on the specific patient search parameter. FHIR-36674 is a broad R5 search-parameter registry alignment issue, and FHIR-56547 plus the 2023 Zulip follow-up show newer compartment questions around AppointmentResponse/patient-vs-subject remain unresolved and outside this seed.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active Appointment search-parameter bundle defines Appointment-patient as a reference parameter targeting Patient with expression Appointment.participant.actor.where(resolve() is Patient) | Appointment.subject.where(resolve() is Patient), and also defines Appointment-subject.

related_jiras.note: Resolved-No-Change PA issue confirms Appointment keeps participant modeling and relies on the patient search parameter for explicit patient lookup.
Published broad R5 registry alignment issue mentioned Appointment-patient, but it is not a bounded Appointment-only source defect for this seed.
Triaged unresolved AppointmentResponse compartment issue shows newer patient compartment questions are not final source-edit scope here.

evidence_items.learned: Later PA rationale supports the current model: keep participant/subject modeling and rely on the patient search parameter for simple lookup.
